newsitem.title: USA: Allied sees Ryder deal adding to earnings.
newsitem.headline: Allied sees Ryder deal adding to earnings.

text.p: Allied Holdings Inc on Wednesday said it expected its pending $114.5 million acquisition of a vehicle-transportation business from Ryder System Inc to add to earnings immediately.
In May, Decatur, Georgia-based Allied Holdings said it planned to acquire Ryder Automotive Carrier Services Inc and Ryder Carrier Management Corp from Ryder System.
Allied executives did not quantify the amount of additional earnings to be generated by the acquisition, which is expected to close in September.
But "significant cost savings" are expected, they added.

"There will be a substantial consolidation of the corporate facilities," A. Mitchell Poole Jr., the company's president, said in an interview. "About 20 terminal locations will either be combined or in some other form merged."
After the acquisition, Allied Holdings will move to the top spot in the market for transporting new cars, with about a 50 percent share. Currently it is in the No. 2 position.
Allied, with a specialized fleet of automotive carriers, said the Ryder acquisition would expand its coverage across North America.
The combined revenue of the Allied and Ryder automotive carrier divisions for 1996 would have been about $1.0 billion. Allied posted 1996 revenues of $392.5 million.
Allied expects to finance the acquisition with a long-term debt offering and may later make a secondary equity offering, depending on favorable market conditions.

"We'd like to eventually see the stock get to a point where we would do another equity offer," Poole said. "We certainly would anticipate doing that when it gets to an appropriate level," Poole said. "
He said proceeds from an equity offering would be used to repay bank debt.
Allied Holdings shares were down 3/8 at 10-1/4 late Wednesday afternoon.
